verdict.rationale: Lium's own pod-creation settings let a user set a single kind of rule: a time limit, end time or USD spend cap, after which the pod is deleted automatically (also exposed as `--ttl` on the CLI). Beyond this fixed auto-termination, there is no general rules engine for linking user-chosen events to user-chosen actions. The availability WebSocket is only a building block a developer would have to wire up, so it earns no credit. Missing for 10: general user-definable event→action rules, triggers beyond time and spend thresholds, configurable actions other than pod deletion, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Pick one, and the pod is deleted when it is reached: Hours... End time... Spend cap: a budget in USD
